253.d:
What lies unseen beneath the black ?

“Maale-Witz” by Antti Pussinen is a boolean conceptual generative NFT painting. 

With colourful brush strokes, a painting is created. The algorithmic artist ponders for a bit and decides to take a more conceptual approach: The painting is painted over with black. What was before, still exist, but invisible.  


“Maale-Witz” offers the viewer two options: either keep the expressionistic painting by clicking on the image within 4 seconds after painting has been finished or see the colours disappear giving the viewer the conceptual black square. 



Features:
Number of brush strokes [90,120,150,180,210,240,270,300]
Colour spectrum width [Monochrome(4.9%),Narrow(27%),Mid(23%),Wide(32%,Very Wide(11,1%)

A visual only feature: If some colour remains visible from under the edge of black, the artwork can be considered rare.

Test outputs can be seen at 
www.twitter.com/antti_pussinen/status/1460906974657318912

279.d:
clickable!

Our second generative token art. Questioning the immortality of data and how it can be corrupted with even the simple click of a button.

This piece allows you to scan the QR code to see the hash that has created it. Every piece is unique due to the way QR codes are generated.

Features influence by the hash are:

- The QR code and its pixel arrangement itself
- The color palette of the QR code (7 variations)
- The background color (5 variations)
- The way the pixel fly around after clicking (4 variations)
- And lastly whether the pixels scale while flying around, creating the illusion of depth (boolean)

GT by Ahmad Moussa || Gorilla Sun
Twitter -> @gorillasu

Notes on randomness and rarity:
This token generates a random permutation of a transmission. A transmission consists of a set of points (interceptors) that a diagonally spanned across the canvas, and connected with lines.
These interceptors can sometimes occur in a square shape.
Sometimes the signal fails to connect two dots, the amount of drops in these connections makes up the decomposition parameter.
The colored ligaments come in a variety of colors, and sometimes the entire transmission has a different color scheme. Some color schemes are extremely rare.

Notes on posting to Twitter:
To make Twitter display these correctly and not harshly compress them, they're best saved in the .jpg or .jpeg format and then posted.

348.d:
An homage to Josef Albers' Homage to the Square, these 100 generative tokens contain grids of 5x5 to 10x10 albersquares (my term for his form). 

Albers' original paintings composed a series of solid color combinations in squares of decreasing volume superimposed on top of one other, each smaller square sitting at regular offset from the center of the larger square. In Albers’ Homages, the squares were shifted down along the y-axis; as in the originals, these albersquares primarily contain down-shifted squares, but 5% are shifted up, 5% are shifted right, 5% left, and 5% centered.

The coloring for each individual square is randomly assigned out of a palette of 30 total colors based on a sampling of Homage to the Square paintings in the Metropolitan Museum of Art archive, with the exception of 5% of all tokens that are grayscale.

A kaleidoscope (/kəˈlaɪdəskoʊp/) is an optical instrument with two or more reflecting surfaces (or mirrors) tilted to each other at an angle, so that one or more (parts of) objects on one end of the mirrors are seen as a regular symmetrical pattern when viewed from the other end, due to repeated reflection. The reflectors are usually enclosed in a tube, often containing on one end a cell with loose, colored pieces of glass or other transparent (and/or opaque) materials to be reflected into the viewed pattern. Rotation of the cell causes motion of the materials, resulting in an ever-changing view being presented.

this is the upgrade version of my Kalley do Scope.
with more pattern and draw line.

tap/click 1 time to reset and draw new line.

when you think you got your best Kalley do Scope,
tap/click 2 times a.k.a double click to save image to your local storage.

or doing nothing and see the loop endlessly.

401.d:
"*Re^iTheta" (pronounced "Starry Eye Theta”) generates patterns with an Iterated Function System parameterized by a single complex number given in polar form as Z =Re^(iTheta), where the two parameters R and Theta are randomly chosen according to the fxhash. The pattern is constructed by joining lines between the sequence of points in the plane defined by taking the number Z and consecutively multiplying it by itself 500 times. The resulting shape is then colored with two randomly chosen complementary colors such that adjacent regions differ in color. The points are then modulated for dynamic effect.

R describes a "contraction" factor in the range: 0.96 < R < 0.98

Theta describes a relative "angle" in the range (radians): 0.785 < Theta < 2.984

Parameter values are divided into three levels according to their magnitude, where "low" and "mid" levels are equally likely and "high" levels occur with a 20% chance.

**click/touch** the Canvas to dynamically generate the pattern through the sequence of points.

487.d:
This algorithm draws inspiration from the wall drawings of Tom Sachs and Sol Lewitt and follows these rules:

* Do as many push-ups as you can to fatigue your arms to the point of failure.
* Then draw a line as close as you can to the one above it without touching.
* If you touch the line above, your turn is over.
* If you lift your pencil, your turn is over.
* If you get to the end of the canvas, your turn is over.


*****


"But at the end of the week, or month, or however long it took to do this wall drawing, you have an expression of your work. And that information, whether you call it beautiful or not… You can’t deny that it is art. Art is art. Good, bad or indifferent, you can’t stop reality from being real. That was Marcel Duchamp and Flavor Flav in one sentence."

-- Tom Sachs on Sol Lewitt's wall drawings.
